decisions.context: Initial website implementation for a local association.
options: static HTML/CSS/JS
framework-based SPA
CMS with hosted backend
decisions.chosen: static HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript
decisions.reason: W0 content site; no backend or dynamic data required; zero paid dependencies and minimal attack surface.
decisions.tradeoffs: Manual source editing instead of CMS authoring workflow.
decisions.evidence: No package dependencies; local static preview.

decisions.context: Unverified current venue and conflicting historical address.
options: publish latest reported address
publish older venue
omit address pending verification
decisions.chosen: omit street address; ask visitors to contact association
decisions.reason: Sources disagree; latest reported suffix conflicts with older municipal/press sources.

decisions.context: Opening times in older sources only.
options: reuse historical Wednesday/Saturday times
omit current schedule
decisions.chosen: omit fixed weekly times
decisions.reason: Current validity not demonstrated.
decisions.risk: HIGH if outdated details misdirect visitors.

decisions.context: Potentially sensitive participant audience.
options: build intake form
email-first contact
collect diagnosis info
decisions.chosen: email-first CTA; no form or diagnosis question
decisions.reason: No business need to collect sensitive personal data online in v1.

decisions.context: No official visual identity supplied.
options: invent official logo
provisional typographic identity and CSS art
decisions.chosen: provisional wordmark and abstract CSS illustration
decisions.reason: Creates coherent presentation without claiming official logo status.

decisions.context: The document-level Escape handler previously always closed the menu and focused its toggle, even when the menu was already closed.
options: Always focus the trigger on Escape
Ignore Escape when the menu is closed; restore focus only when dismissing an open menu
decisions.chosen: Ignore Escape unless aria-expanded is true; restore focus only after closing an open menu.
decisions.reason: Avoids unexpected focus movement to a hidden trigger on desktop and while the mobile menu is already closed.
decisions.tradeoffs: The key handler is state-aware and has a dedicated dependency-free regression test.
decisions.evidence: node tests/test_menu.js passes against the actual script.js.

decisions.context: CR-001 expands informational requirements and photo/motion direction.
options: Leave contract 0.1 active
Adopt evidence-derived contract 0.2 in authorized Loop 003
decisions.chosen: Adopt Product Contract 0.2 as active evidence-derived baseline, not human-approved.
decisions.reason: The exact CONTINUE authorized Loop 003 following CR-001; requirements are traceable and use conservative factual framing.
decisions.reversibility: Versioned contract and Git history preserve 0.1.

decisions.context: The request calls for more imagery but real participant photos are not cleared.
options: Reuse social/press photos
Use local original non-identifying SVG illustrations pending permission
decisions.chosen: Use original local SVG illustrations clearly labelled as illustrations.
decisions.reason: Public visibility is not publication permission, especially for minors and vulnerable people.
decisions.reversibility: Replace with approved documentary imagery after rights/consent clearance.

decisions.context: Scroll animations may affect accessibility or essential content visibility.
options: Hide content until animation fires
Use progressive IntersectionObserver enhancement with reduced-motion/unsupported fallback
decisions.chosen: Progressive reveal; only apply hidden initial state when observer is supported and reduced motion is off.
decisions.reason: Content remains visible without JavaScript/observer and respects reduced-motion preferences.
decisions.reversibility: Remove enhancement without altering content structure.

decisions.context: User requested shorter sections, less generic typography, a professional design and a stronger visual background.
options: Retain the image-heavy pastel cards and long story mosaic
Consolidate duplicate content into a concise editorial five-section page with a restrained palette and typographic hierarchy
decisions.chosen: Consolidate into five sections: hero, activities, welcome/first contact, APAiL, contact.
decisions.reason: The previous design repeated welcome/approach/first-step/volunteer content and relied heavily on generic repeated illustration cards. A concise editorial layout better communicates the documented welcome/listening ethos with less scrolling.
decisions.tradeoffs: Dated social-post mosaic and decorative placeholder illustrations are removed; fewer visual story details are displayed.
decisions.evidence: Loop 006 structural validator, Chromium viewport sweep and screenshots.

decisions.context: The user supplied the exact Bulle Bleue - APAiL Facebook page as a potential official brand source.
options: Use a different-ID third-party mirror as if it were the supplied page
Link the exact user-supplied page, but defer logo/photo reuse until that exact page's assets can be verified
decisions.chosen: Add the exact Facebook URL in contact and footer; do not copy an unverified logo or photographs.
decisions.reason: The supplied page URL was blocked by the fetch environment. A public mirror surfaced a different page ID (100620708811103 versus the supplied 100066715807933), so identity cannot be assumed.
decisions.tradeoffs: The current BB monogram and palette remain provisional; official artwork is still unverified.
decisions.evidence: Direct attempt to open user-provided Facebook URL; FindGlocal mirror ID comparison.

decisions.context: A distinctive display/body type system should remain free of paid services and avoid unnecessary third-party requests.
options: Load remote font APIs
Use an editorial font stack with platform fallback and no remote font request
decisions.chosen: Use EB Garamond/Cabin when available, with Iowan Old Style, Palatino, Georgia, Avenir Next, Segoe UI and other local system fallbacks.
decisions.reason: No paid service or remote font request is required; the Chromium environment confirmed both named faces are locally available.
decisions.tradeoffs: Rendering may fall back to a platform font on visitor devices where EB Garamond or Cabin is not installed; cross-platform fallback inspection remains outstanding.
decisions.evidence: Chromium 144 document.fonts checks and CSS source inspection.

decisions.context: The user supplied a complete Markdown extraction from the exact Bulle Bleue - APAiL Facebook page and asked to replace website content using it.
options: Keep Loop 006 generic copy
Use supplied extraction as primary source with explicit source/date caveats
Publish every post as a long chronology
decisions.chosen: Replace the page with a concise source-led structure covering audience, times, venue, activities, dated highlights, APAiL history/solidarity, volunteers, cited organisations and contact.
decisions.reason: The extraction identifies the exact page and covers May 2023 through October 2026. The user explicitly directed that it be used as the primary content source.
decisions.tradeoffs: The content is richer than Loop 006 but curated rather than copied verbatim. Venue and session validity cannot be guaranteed from the document alone.
decisions.evidence: Bulle_Bleue_APAiL_contenu_facebook.md (blob dec4ee6c3f4e0ea7c092ebe1760c4a35033e05bf), Loop 007 index.html and updated validator.

decisions.context: The user requested a more organised professional site, with the homepage no longer containing everything.
options: Keep a long single-page site with anchor navigation
Split major topics into dedicated pages with common navigation
Introduce a CMS or SPA
decisions.chosen: Six static HTML pages: home, La Bulle, activities, news, APAiL and contact.
decisions.reason: Each major visitor question now has a dedicated, predictable destination; the homepage acts as an index. Static files preserve zero paid dependencies and simple hosting.
decisions.tradeoffs: Shared navigation and common footer must remain consistent across separate files; automated tests now enforce this.
decisions.evidence: Loop 009 multi-page validator and route source review.

decisions.context: The user supplied the official transparent logo and documentary photographs, and reports owner authorization for Facebook-page assets.
options: Keep the provisional BB monogram and no documentary photos
Use the official logo and publish a full gallery of all uploaded photos
Use the official logo and a small selection of non-identifying activity close-ups while deferring identifiable portraits
decisions.chosen: Replace the BB monogram with the official logo in all six headers and footers; use four local close-up photographs on the homepage and activities page; defer photos showing identifiable participants.
decisions.reason: The four selected photos show games and activities without identifiable faces. The other supplied photos contain identifiable people, including children. The user-reported owner permission is recorded, while participant/guardian release status is not independently documented.
decisions.tradeoffs: The exact logo palette cannot yet be sampled from the supplied >1 MB PNG; existing CSS colour tokens remain explicitly provisional until a direct visual sample is available.
decisions.evidence: Loop 010 source audit, asset register and user-supplied repository files.

decisions.context: The user's main brand requirement is for the site's full colour system to come from the official logo, but the available repository reader could not return the PNG binary.
options: Guess a palette and describe it as logo-derived
Retain the existing tokenized palette as provisional and defer exact calibration until the logo can be visually sampled
decisions.chosen: Retain the existing tokenized colours as provisional and explicitly block exact palette sign-off.
decisions.reason: A 1,062,882-byte PNG produced an empty response from the repository file reader; no trustworthy pixel sampling was possible. Guessing would falsely claim that the site palette was derived from the logo.
decisions.tradeoffs: The logo and photos are integrated, but the requested final colour-led artistic direction remains incomplete.
decisions.evidence: GitHub asset blob 82c6eb3e5067b19ebb94c356723f8ad05b8cbde9; repeated base64/UTF-8 retrieval attempts returned no PNG payload.

decisions.context: Loop 011 received the original transparent logo as an inspectable uploaded image, making the previously blocked logo-palette task possible.
options: Retain the inherited warm clay/ochre palette
Choose blue shades by visual guess
Extract dominant representative colours from visible logo pixels and use them as shared design tokens
decisions.chosen: Use an alpha-weighted eight-cluster sample of visible RGBA logo pixels; the primary token family is navy #06195E, cobalt #1642A5, primary blue #1C60CF, clear blue #2084DE, sky blue #4EABEC, steel blue #587ABA, icy blue #9DC0EA and pale highlight #D3DEF0.
decisions.reason: The upload is RGBA with a transparent background; colour clusters were computed from non-transparent pixels using a reproducible deterministic sample. Hex values are the nearest actual image pixel to cluster centres. Surface whites are documented tints, not falsely labelled as sampled logo pixels.
decisions.tradeoffs: Blue-focused art direction will replace the former warm paper/clay/gold identity; the content and typography remain unchanged.
decisions.evidence: Uploaded logo final.png (1052×1024 RGBA); alpha-weighted KMeans analysis, Loop 011 CSS tokens and source audit.

decisions.context: The site needs legible page surfaces while remaining visibly derived from the highly saturated blue logo.
options: Use saturated logo colours for every page background
Use logo blues for identity and accents, with very pale derived tints for long-reading surfaces
decisions.chosen: Use sampled deep navy/cobalt/blue shades for headings, hero fields, links and accents; use derived near-white tints #F3F7FE and #FCFDFF for reading surfaces; use #D3DEF0 for pale section fields.
decisions.reason: This preserves the logo colour character while maintaining text legibility and a calm professional informational site.
decisions.tradeoffs: Near-white tints are blended derivatives of the logo highlight, not colours sampled verbatim from image pixels.
decisions.evidence: Logo-derived palette and CSS contrast checks.

decisions.context: The owner requested a simpler and more predictable top-level menu with distinct pages for identity, news, membership, contact and legal notices.
options: Keep the six-page menu and expose every previous category
Consolidate previous La Bulle, Activities and APAiL information on Qui sommes-nous, add Adhérer and legal page, retain Actualités and Contact
decisions.chosen: Five primary destinations: Accueil, Qui sommes-nous ?, Actualités, Adhérer, Nous contacter; Mentions légales is a shared footer link. Previous La Bulle, Activités and APAiL files are replaced by one consolidated Qui sommes-nous page.
decisions.reason: Matches the owner's explicit information architecture and avoids duplicate or fragmented content.
decisions.evidence: User feedback dated 2026-11-03; Loop 012 route and navigation source audit.

decisions.context: The owner wants a drawn background that remains visible while homepage text changes during scrolling.
options: Keep a separate photo hero and static destination mosaic
Use a sticky local illustration with progressive scroll chapters
Use remote video/background service
decisions.chosen: A single original local SVG scene is sticky behind three text chapters; IntersectionObserver switches the active copy.
decisions.reason: No paid or remote dependencies are needed; reduced-motion and no-observer fallbacks leave all copy visible.
decisions.tradeoffs: Sticky behavior and timing still require rendered browser review.
decisions.evidence: Loop 012 index.html, styles.css, script.js and interaction regression test.

decisions.context: The Actualités page is a high-priority user journey and the source offers only dated summaries with no direct post permalink mapping for the stored illustrations.
options: List a long textual chronology
Show two or three cards without article details
Show exactly three curated cards, each with a dedicated article and clearly labelled representative illustration
decisions.chosen: Three dated cards with three root-level article pages; original SVG illustrations are explicitly described as illustrations and not photographs of the events.
decisions.reason: Matches the owner's requested news-site interaction without misrepresenting the image-to-event relationship.
decisions.evidence: Supplied Facebook extraction for 2026-10-26, 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-10; Loop 012 pages.

decisions.context: The owner requested Adhérer and Mentions légales pages but current membership and legal configuration details are not evidenced.
options: Invent fees/legal entities/host information
Leave both pages absent
Provide functional contact guidance and visibly pending legal fields without inventing details
decisions.chosen: Adhérer routes to an email request for the current terms. Mentions légales is a clearly marked draft with unknown publisher, registered-office, publication manager and host details pending confirmation.
decisions.reason: Complies with AEOS no-invention rule and avoids collecting personal data before a verified process exists.
decisions.evidence: Available supplied extraction, project.config.json and Loop 012 content review.

decisions.context: The user asked that the photographs they supplied be used on the site while the homepage retains the owner's sticky illustrated scroll-story.
options: Replace the illustrated story background with Facebook photographs
Use the supplied people-forward group photographs throughout the site
Keep the sticky illustration and add a restrained gallery using close-up activity photographs without recognizable faces
decisions.chosen: Keep the sticky SVG story background and add two user-supplied close-up tabletop activity photographs in a separate homepage gallery.
decisions.reason: This incorporates the supplied documentary assets without misrepresenting their connection to dated articles or publishing recognizable participant/children images without image-specific releases.
decisions.tradeoffs: Only two selected close-ups are used in this loop; other supplied photographs remain archived pending image-specific release confirmation.
decisions.evidence: The selected files were visually inspected directly: the frames show game boards, pieces and hands, with no recognizable faces; asset register and homepage validator were updated.

decisions.context: Direct visual inspection of the Loop 014 CI screenshots showed two capture defects: lazy gallery images were not loaded in screenshot navigations, and a sticky-story panel was captured while its opacity transition was still in progress. Full-page screenshots also represented sticky artwork poorly because they expand the capture viewport rather than simulating user scrolling.
options: Treat automated screenshots as already trustworthy because browser image/scroll assertions passed
Disable lazy loading or remove story transitions from the website

Keep the live experience unchanged and make screenshot capture explicitly load/decode gallery assets, capture each story state in the viewport after its transition completes, and avoid misleading full-page sticky captures
decisions.chosen: Keep the user-facing experience and fix the visual-evidence process: wait for each story panel to be fully visible, decode lazy images, and capture three desktop story states plus desktop/mobile gallery views.
decisions.reason: The issue is in screenshot capture timing and full-page sticky rendering, not evidence that the actual user-facing scroll behavior is broken. Lazy loading remains appropriate for the public page.
decisions.tradeoffs: The CI artifact grows from three to six screenshots and remains short-retention.
decisions.evidence: Direct inspection of Loop 014 artifact 13241331764 showed blank gallery placeholders in captures and a near-transparent final story panel; screenshot source was then audited against IntersectionObserver and lazy-loading behavior.

decisions.context: Public legal/association records now provide a JOAFE-published denomination and RNA/SIREN identifiers, but the registered-office address differs across public sources.
options: Continue to show all legal identity details as unknown
Select one public address and present it as the current registered office
Publish the sourced JOAFE denomination and registry identifiers, retain the address as pending, and disclose the record conflict
decisions.chosen: Use the name published in the 27 February 2019 JOAFE modification notice and list RNA W712002504 / SIREN 519 970 743 as registry identifiers with an association-confirmation note. Do not select a current registered-office address while the public records conflict.
decisions.reason: This resolves verifiable identity details without converting an activity/directory address or potentially stale record into a legal claim about the current registered office.
decisions.tradeoffs: The legal page is more informative but still cannot be signed off until APAiL confirms the address, publication manager and hosting provider.
decisions.evidence: Official JOAFE announcement 20190009/1308; Ville de Chalon association directory; public RNA/SIRENE-derived listing updated 2026-06-24.

decisions.context: The association owner explicitly rejected rigid rectangles and asked for a joyful, childlike, arts-led design across the whole website.
options: Keep the restrained professional editorial system
Use rounded corners only on selected cards
Adopt a consistent playful design language with irregular bubble geometry, pill actions, informal local typography and supporting pastel accents
decisions.chosen: Adopt the playful, arts-led visual direction across all nine public pages while retaining the supplied blue logo as the identity anchor.
decisions.reason: This directly reflects the owner's feedback; local system fonts preserve the zero-remote-dependency policy and readability.
decisions.tradeoffs: The informal font will vary by device; final owner visual acceptance remains necessary.
decisions.evidence: Owner feedback dated 2026-11-05 and Loop 017 CSS implementation.

decisions.context: The owner asked to replace the homepage placeholder art with the five drawings uploaded in the repository.
options: Keep the SVG placeholder
Use only the panorama
Create a layered collage from all five user-supplied drawings
decisions.chosen: Use all five drawings in an organic, sticker-like collage behind the three sticky story chapters.
decisions.reason: It makes the children's artwork the centre of the visual identity and fulfils the exact asset request.
decisions.tradeoffs: Image cropping/placement is responsive CSS and requires visual review on multiple viewports.
decisions.evidence: Direct visual inspection of all five JPEGs and exact main-branch asset paths.

decisions.context: The owner supplied all photo assets and the project user clarified that the association owner verbally authorised their visible use on the website.
options: Exclude people-forward photos until additional written releases are collected
Use only close-up activity photos
Treat the owner's verbal permission as the project authorization and include the entire supplied image set
decisions.chosen: Accept the association owner's verbal website-use authorization, as relayed by the user, and include all eleven assets/posts photographs plus gathering.jpeg.
decisions.reason: The owner supplied the photos and directly authorized their use. The project now treats this verbal authorization as sufficient and does not impose an additional permission gate.
decisions.tradeoffs: The owner remains responsible for the association's supplied content and its authorization; the website describes photographs without naming individuals.
decisions.evidence: User clarification on 2026-11-05: owner supplied all images and verbally authorized visible website use; all relevant paths are committed in the repository.

decisions.context: The user clarified that all eleven assets/posts photos should not crowd the homepage; only gathering.jpeg belongs in the closing section.
options: Keep all eleven in the homepage gallery
Remove all assets/posts photos
Distribute eight activity photos to Qui sommes-nous and three undated group/outing photos to Actualités
decisions.chosen: Keep the homepage light with gathering.jpeg only; place eight activity photos on Qui sommes-nous and three group/outing photos in a separate, undated Actualités image strip.
decisions.reason: The activities belong beside the activity description, while group/outing moments enrich a general community image strip without falsely associating them with dated news. The homepage returns to a clear story-first flow.
decisions.tradeoffs: Secondary pages become richer; alt text and responsive layouts must stay concise.
decisions.evidence: User clarification during Loop 018 and direct inspection of all eleven assets.

decisions.context: The Actualités cards still read as rectangles, and pastel page headers rendered near-white text while the solidarity panel combined a dark gradient with dark text.
options: Make small border-radius adjustments only
Use a coherent palette and organic card silhouettes with explicit contrast roles
decisions.chosen: Redesign news cards with asymmetrical bubble/blob pseudo-surfaces and curved image frames; use deep navy/blue text on pale pastel surfaces and light text only on dark blue panels.
decisions.reason: The user explicitly asked for articles that look like bubbles and readable colour choices; this resolves the identified mismatched background/text pairings.
decisions.tradeoffs: Large organic card shapes need desktop/mobile visual review.
decisions.evidence: Direct CSS audit in Loop 018 and browser checks of computed styles.

decisions.context: The owner supplied precise homepage text, a selected Se retrouver group photo, new drawings, an activity-layout HTML reference and exact font preferences.
options: Keep current homepage copy and old typography
Adopt owner text/artwork/fonts while preserving the approved secondary-page photo distribution
decisions.chosen: Implement the owner-approved homepage sequence and wording, use supplied drawings and selected photograph, adapt the four-artwork collage, and apply Fredoka/Atkinson Hyperlegible/Caveat.
decisions.reason: The owner feedback is direct and specific; the implementation must express the association's voice while preserving the airy homepage and honest provenance.
decisions.tradeoffs: Google Fonts CSS becomes a free runtime font request; system fallbacks protect legibility. Separate character extraction remains pending.
decisions.evidence: CR-012, owner-uploaded images and supplied section-jouer-creer.html.

decisions.context: Only one real testimonial was provided, while the requested visual layout has three cards for young people, parents and volunteers.
options: Invent sample testimonials
Show Miette's authentic quote and mark the remaining cards as invitations
decisions.chosen: Use only Miette's verified owner-supplied quotation; other cards remain explicit 'Témoignage à recueillir' invitations with no attributed words.
decisions.reason: Attribution must remain truthful. The page can invite future contributions without claiming statements that have not been provided.
decisions.tradeoffs: The three supporting cards are invitation prompts rather than quotations until real material is supplied.
decisions.evidence: Owner feedback received 2026-11-05.

decisions.context: Actualités cards continued to look like rounded rectangles despite asymmetric radii.
options: Continue adjusting radii
Use smooth sampled Bézier contours
decisions.chosen: Use three distinct sampled organic silhouettes with matching clipped illustration frames and safe badge placement.
decisions.reason: The user asked for bubble-shaped news cards; smooth contours create the difference while preserving readable content and responsive layout.
decisions.tradeoffs: Clip-path is progressive enhancement; border-radius remains fallback. Desktop tags move upper-right.
decisions.evidence: Loop 019/020 desktop/mobile screenshot review and Playwright assertions.

decisions.context: Drawings 6–9 were displayed as complete rectangular sheets in the sticky homepage story collage. The owner-feedback TODO requested separate transparent character cut-outs while retaining the original sheets.
options: Keep complete sheets as the only sticky artwork
Create individual transparent cut-outs from the supplied originals while preserving the full sheets in Jouer/créer
Redraw the figures or use generated replacements
decisions.chosen: Create 20 independently addressable SVG cut-outs using manually traced clip paths over the original JPEG pixels; use them as individually positioned figures in the sticky art groups and retain all four complete source drawings in Jouer/créer.
decisions.reason: The user asked for transparent character cut-outs; preserving the supplied image pixels avoids changing child-made artwork and keeps provenance clear. The pasted football photograph and cropped edge fragment in drawing 7 are excluded from the drawn-character set.
decisions.tradeoffs: Silhouette boundaries are hand-traced approximations; external JPEG image references inside the SVGs preserve the source pixels without duplicating the originals. The full drawing sheets remain available as documentary artwork.
decisions.evidence: CR-014, twenty SVG assets, source-preservation structural assertions and Loop 022 Chromium screenshots.

decisions.context: The user requested a fine visual cleanup, especially spacing, leftover numbering and centering. Baseline screenshots showed decorative 01/02 labels on About audience cards, a left-anchored capped-width Adhérer note/legal column, unequal lower callout positions in Contact and misaligned Adhérer actions.
options: Keep the existing micro-layouts unchanged
Apply a focused spacing/alignment polish, remove only decorative audience numbering, and keep historical dates intact
decisions.chosen: Remove About's decorative 01/02 labels, present the audience groups as responsive cards, center Adhérer/legal narrow content columns, align Contact lower callouts and align Adhérer desktop actions; refine page/card spacing and title/metadata baselines.
decisions.reason: The request targets visual finish rather than content redesign. Historical timeline years 1995 and 2021 are factual and remain visible; the numbering removed was decorative sequence chrome only.
decisions.tradeoffs: The Contact and Adhérer callouts are aligned in side-by-side desktop layouts; mobile intentionally stacks them vertically. The original playful editorial visual language and page content are preserved.
decisions.evidence: CR-015, browser assertions, 30 screenshots from Loop 023 CI artifact; seven desktop/mobile captures manually reviewed.

decisions.context: The user reported remaining imperfections, especially on Qui sommes-nous. Review of Loop 023 desktop/mobile screenshots showed that the seven About activity labels were compressed by a legacy divider/list treatment and a fixed-position body background dot floated beside the volunteer section on the long page.
options: Retain the divider and document-positioned circles
Remove the page-level dots and render About topics as separated, individually bordered cards
Replace the About content and add new illustrations
decisions.chosen: Remove the document-level decorative dots while preserving section- and component-attached decoration. Present the seven About activity topics as roomy cards in two columns on wider screens and one column on mobile, without changing their wording.
decisions.reason: The defects were caused by legacy presentation rules rather than content. A narrow scoped override fixes the source of the artefacts while retaining the association's existing playful colour palette and owner-provided content.
decisions.tradeoffs: The body uses its solid warm paper colour instead of fixed-position dot decoration. Intentional decorative shapes on the news cards, illustrations and section backgrounds remain.
decisions.evidence: CR-016, REQ-066, Python validator, Loop 024 Playwright assertions and 30 responsive Chromium captures; six desktop/mobile captures manually reviewed.

decisions.context: The responsive browser regression had only launched Chromium, while Firefox, WebKit/Safari-family and assistive-technology checks remained open.
options: Keep the existing Chromium-only CI suite
Run the same responsive regression in Chromium, Firefox and Playwright WebKit; separately retain native Safari and assistive-technology testing as future checks
decisions.chosen: Make the Playwright engine configurable through BROWSER_ENGINE and run the complete nine-page/five-viewport regression sequentially in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit in GitHub Actions. Keep visual screenshots from Chromium only to avoid duplicate artifacts.
decisions.reason: The same assertions across independent browser engines catch engine-specific CSS serialization, navigation, rendering and interaction differences without changing site content or dependencies. A real Safari/iOS pass cannot be inferred from Playwright WebKit running on Linux.
decisions.tradeoffs: The CI job takes longer and downloads three browser engines. WebKit is Safari-family engine coverage, not native macOS/iOS Safari. Native devices and assistive technology remain separate validation items.
decisions.evidence: CR-017, REQ-067, GitHub Actions run 42237625691; 9 routes × 5 viewport widths × 3 engines; Chromium screenshot artifact 13511744695.
